record.paper_title: Recent progress and open problems in the Bergman space
record.context_brief: Cauchy dual kernels for nonradial measures
record.original_question: Let mu be a positive measure on D such that point evaluation on polynomials is bounded and mu reproduces the origin, integral_D p(z) dmu(z) = p(0) for all polynomials p. Let P^2(mu) be the closure of polynomials in L^2(mu), and define the Cauchy dual as the analytic functions whose boundary Cauchy pairing gives bounded linear functionals on P^2(mu). Is the reproducing kernel of the Cauchy dual of P^2(mu) always a complete Nevanlinna-Pick kernel?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 18 Let mu be a measure as above

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$ denote the open unit disk. Let $\mu$ be a positive Borel measure on $\mathbb{D}$ such that:

(i) point evaluation $p \mapsto p(z_0)$ is bounded on the space of holomorphic polynomials with respect to the $L^2(\mu)$-norm, for every $z_0 \in \mathbb{D}$; and

(ii) $\mu$ reproduces the origin in the sense that $\int_{\mathbb{D}} p(z)\, d\mu(z) = p(0)$ for every holomorphic polynomial $p$.

Let $P^2(\mu)$ be the closure of the holomorphic polynomials in $L^2(\mu)$; it is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space of analytic functions on $\mathbb{D}$. Define the Cauchy dual of $P^2(\mu)$ to be the Hilbert space of analytic functions $g$ on $\mathbb{D}$ for which the Cauchy pairing
$$\langle f, g \rangle_C = \lim_{r \to 1^-} \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} f(re^{i\theta})\,\overline{g(re^{i\theta})}\, d\theta$$
(suitably interpreted via boundary behavior) extends to a bounded linear functional on $P^2(\mu)$, with norm given by the operator norm of this functional. The Cauchy dual is itself a reproducing kernel Hilbert space of analytic functions on $\mathbb{D}$.

Question: Is the reproducing kernel of the Cauchy dual of $P^2(\mu)$ always a complete Nevanlinna–Pick kernel?

(Recall: a positive definite kernel $k$ on a set $X$ is a complete Nevanlinna–Pick kernel if the matrix-valued Pick interpolation theorem holds for the multiplier algebra of the associated reproducing kernel Hilbert space; equivalently, $1 - 1/k(x,y)$ has exactly one positive square after normalization at a basepoint.)
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a definitive resolution of the question of whether the reproducing kernel of the Cauchy dual of $P^2(\mu)$ is always a complete Nevanlinna–Pick kernel for nonradial reproducing measures $\mu$ on the disk. Related literature on complete Nevanlinna–Pick kernels, Bergman-type contractions, and Cauchy duality discusses analogous questions, but no source clearly establishes or refutes this specific statement. The problem appears to remain open, but the evidence is inconclusive.

status_evidence.title: Complete Nevanlinna-Pick Kernels (Agler–McCarthy)
status_evidence.snippet: Characterization of reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces on which the Pick interpolation theorem holds in its full matrix-valued form.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the standard framework for complete Nevanlinna–Pick kernels but does not address the Cauchy dual of $P^2(\mu)$ for general nonradial $\mu$.

status_evidence.title: Complete Nevanlinna-Pick kernels and the characteristic function
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Bergman-type contractions and the characteristic function in the complete Nevanlinna–Pick setting.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work in the area does not resolve the Cauchy-dual NP question for arbitrary reproducing measures.
